name: Posture from Chill Dog
description: Posture recovery from Chill Dog frees the isolated arm and high-leg connection before raising the chest. Keep a balanced base and protect the captured shoulder.
summary: Posture recovery from Chill Dog frees the isolated arm and high-leg connection before the top player raises the chest.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Chill Dog; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. This is defense inside facing rubber guard. Closed or half guard depends on which lower-body connections remain; neither is guaranteed by raising the head.

Keep the free hand available for framing while preventing the isolated elbow from being pulled further away from your torso. The opponent changing the hand around your head signals the move beyond New York, not a turtle escape. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (top): How should your free hand help the trapped arm?
flashcards.answer: The free hand preserves inside space while you prevent the isolated elbow being drawn farther from your ribs.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep an inside frame while the elbow stays compact

plausible: Reach behind their back and flare the elbow
Post both hands wide beyond their hips
trap: Keep the free hand on the mat while pulling the elbow inward

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (top): Which cue identifies their neck-cleared control?
flashcards.answer: Chill Dog changes the head-side hand and forearm position while retaining the New York arm isolation.
flashcards.answer_line: Their head-side arm has circled around your head

plausible: Their hand has only begun lifting your wrist
Their ankles are crossed low around your waist
trap: Their knee hug closes before any head-side grip change

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (top): What should support the early escape attempt?
flashcards.answer: Use early inside space with stable supports while the neck and shoulder are still free enough to move.
flashcards.answer_line: A balanced base and an inside forearm

plausible: A narrow base with both hands behind their back
An extended arm pinned outside their knee
trap: A wide knee base with the free forearm outside the shoulder

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (top): Where should you seek slack before lifting posture?
flashcards.answer: Open the high-leg attachment while keeping head and shoulder aligned before trying to lift the chest.
flashcards.answer_line: At the high leg's hip-and-thigh connection

plausible: Only at your free wrist while the leg stays tight
Only at the floor by widening your knees
trap: At their free foot while the controlling leg stays tight

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (top): What happens before the chest rises?
flashcards.answer: Free the shoulder and recover the elbow toward your ribs through slack before lifting upright.
flashcards.answer_line: The isolated elbow returns through the opened leg

plausible: Raise the chest while leaving the elbow outside their knee
Withdraw the free inside frame before opening the high leg
trap: Pull the head upward while the knee hug still holds the arm

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (top): Head free, their ankles crossed behind your waist: what remains?
flashcards.answer: Posture recovery changes upper-body control. With the opponent's ankles crossed behind your waist, closed guard still remains; a free head does not complete a pass. Check the actual leg relationship rather than inferring a destination from the posture change.

plausible: Half guard trapping one of your thighs
Side control beyond both of their knees
trap: Open guard with their feet separated

flashcards.question: Chill Dog posture recovery: which starting enclosure must you escape?
flashcards.answer: The top player is freeing the head and arm from a bottom-player leg-and-arm clinch, not removing their own rear hooks.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing high guard with an isolated arm and neck clearance

plausible: Their low crossed ankles with both arms framing inside
Their second-leg closure with no arm isolated
trap: Their head clasp after both high legs have lowered

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (top): What separates posturing from passing here?
flashcards.answer: A free head and elbow allow posture, but passing also requires moving beyond the guard player's remaining leg barriers.
flashcards.answer_line: The remaining knees and hips still need clearance

plausible: The inside elbow has already cleared their near knee
Head height determines whether the far hip is passed
trap: Shoulder pressure replaces clearing the remaining leg hook

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (top): Your shoulder cannot move in the hug; what comes first?
flashcards.answer: A fixed shoulder must be released before elbow extraction; stop if joint pressure is already being applied.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the arm-and-leg connection before pulling back

plausible: Pull farther until the elbow passes the knee
Raise the chest first to stretch the loop
trap: Draw only the wrist in while the knee hug stays tight

defender.name: Posture from Chill Dog Defender
defender.description: Posture from Chill Dog (defender): Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip. Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Chill Dog; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. This is defense inside facing rubber guard. Closed or half guard depends on which lower-body connections remain; neither is guaranteed by raising the head.

Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip. Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee. Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.

Use the forearm near the shoulder line to manage forward pressure; do not let the frame collapse across your own wrist. Keep the knee hug while choosing further control such as Invisible Collar or an omoplata setup. Return the legs to a comfortable guard if the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

If the high control opens, switch to guard retention with an inside shoulder frame and hip movement that returns a knee. Do not chase the head while the top player advances chest pressure into the space left by the falling leg.
key_principles: Secure New York first: Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip.
Turn onto the hip: Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee.
Clear the neck: Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.
Place the inside frame: Use the forearm near the shoulder line to manage forward pressure; do not let the frame collapse across your own wrist.
Maintain the arm trap: Keep the knee hug while choosing further control such as Invisible Collar or an omoplata setup.
Recover when control opens: Return the legs to a comfortable guard if the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back.
recognition_cues: The top player faces a bottom guard player using Chill Dog; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed.
The opponent changing the hand around your head signals the move beyond New York, not a turtle escape.
Create slack at the hip and thigh while keeping the head and captured arm aligned.

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (bottom): What denies their elbow an easy return inside?
flashcards.answer: The connected arm wrap and knee support retain New York isolation while the opponent attempts to recover posture.
flashcards.answer_line: Your overhook with the knee hugged over the arm

plausible: Only a grip on the back of their head
A free foot on their hip with the arm uncovered
trap: A knee held high after the overhook has loosened

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (bottom): How can you support the high leg as they lift?
flashcards.answer: Use hip angle and knee support to retain posture control while it remains comfortable; avoid pulling a distant foot.
flashcards.answer_line: Bring the knee forward by adjusting the hip

plausible: Stay flat and haul the ankle toward your face
Let the knee drift backward while gripping higher
trap: Raise the ankle first and leave the knee behind

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (bottom): What should remain cleared during their posture attempt?
flashcards.answer: Retain the cleared head-side connection along with the arm trap; allowing the head back inside can undo the Chill Dog checkpoint.
flashcards.answer_line: The head-side arm position around their head

plausible: Their trapped hand moving onto your chest
Your forearm sliding outside their returning shoulder
trap: Your knee hug alone while the head-side grip returns across

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (bottom): Where does your forearm resist their return to center?
flashcards.answer: The inside forearm acts as a supported barrier against the opponent returning their head and shoulder into the space.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside near their shoulder and collarbone

plausible: Outside the shoulder with your wrist folded
Along their outer upper arm with your elbow away
trap: Against their collarbone with your wrist folded beneath it

flashcards.question: Posture from Chill Dog (bottom): Their elbow is free and the high leg falls; what now?
flashcards.answer: Switch to guard retention as the old control opens, using the frame and hip movement to rebuild knee space.
flashcards.answer_line: Recover a knee behind an inside shoulder frame

plausible: Keep reaching for the head with both hands
Leave the fallen leg outside while holding the wrist
trap: Regrip the fallen ankle before recovering the near knee
